title: Lab 3: Optical Finger PPG (LED + Photoresistor)
author: Bioelectrical Lab Sim Demo
description: Build an optical photoplethysmography (PPG) sensor using a powered Red LED and a CdS Photoresistor voltage divider, then stream the arterial pulse to the Arduino Nano Serial Plotter.

steps.title: Build the Optical Light Source (Red LED)
steps.instruction: Place an Arduino Nano, a 330 Ω resistor, and a Red LED powered from the Nano's +5 V and GND pins. Remember: the photoresistor PPG mode will NOT detect a pulse without a lit LED!
steps.hint: Connect Nano 5V -> 330 Ω -> Red LED Anode (+), and LED Cathode (−) -> Nano GND.

steps.title: Wire the Photoresistor Voltage Divider to A0
steps.instruction: Place a Photoresistor (CdS LDR) and a 10 kΩ resistor in a +5 V to GND voltage divider, and connect the midpoint to Arduino Nano pin A0.
steps.hint: Wire +5 V -> Photoresistor -> midpoint strip -> 10 kΩ -> GND, then run a jumper from the midpoint strip to Nano A0.

steps.title: Enable LED + Finger PPG Mode
steps.instruction: Click the Photoresistor on the breadboard to open its inspector, switch from Manual Light to LED + Finger PPG, and toggle Finger Interposed ON.
steps.hint: You should see a cyan pulse halo appear on the photoresistor and the badge 'LED Linked · Finger PPG' in the inspector.

checks.label: Photoresistor set to LED + Finger PPG mode
Finger interposed between LED and LDR

steps.title: Sample & Plot the PPG Pulse on Arduino Nano
steps.instruction: Open the Nano tab, choose or write a sketch that reads analogRead(A0) and prints to Serial, click Upload & Run, and inspect the beating waveform in the Serial Plotter.
steps.hint: Try the built-in 'Optical PPG (LED + Photoresistor)' sketch from the Example Sketches dropdown, then remove the 330 Ω resistor to confirm the PPG flatlines without the LED!

checks.label: Arduino sketch running & streaming Serial data
I verified the PPG disappears when the Red LED is turned off
